disposition_reason: FAST has an ordered temporal-fidelity comparison, but the exact numeric source baseline and pixel/ROI/synchronization recipe for the registered real recordings are not recovered. The existing evaluator deliberately uses a prospective group-disjoint recipe, which changes the original same-stack self-supervised task and cannot award a source-paper win. Published throughput alone is not a substitute for denoising quality.

source_paper.title: Real-time self-supervised denoising for high-speed fluorescence neural imaging

evidence.locator: Figure 3b,d–f and voltage-imaging Results; Figure 1d; Methods: Training and inference
evidence.supports: Defines synthetic spike-width controls, real 1000-Hz QuasAr6a electrophysiology comparison, pixel-level correlations and source same-stack training; separately reports hardware-bound throughput.

evidence.locator: Quick Start; Configuration; Training and inference guide
evidence.supports: Pinned executable author route and configuration: model/checkpoint workflow, 100 epochs, seed 123, and code configuration values requiring reconciliation with paper Methods.

evidence.locator: goTesting, temporal output accumulation and image saving
evidence.supports: Author temporal-window inference and output handling must be preserved and audited against original frame support.

evidence.locator: Scientific basis and prospective choices; Provenance and preserved discrepancies
evidence.supports: Existing evaluator declares new ROI/F0/group-split rules, uses synthetic-only image error, and explicitly excludes native test-stack adaptation; it is an extension and measurement component.

target.description: Denoise the original neural fluorescence recordings while preserving fast voltage/calcium dynamics and source real-time constraints. The real voltage fidelity endpoint compares denoised pixel fluorescence traces with simultaneous electrophysiology, not with a fabricated clean fluorescence image.

dataset.description: Source raw data are deposited at Zenodo 15872025; Figure 3d–f uses a QuasAr6a-expressing cortical neuron and simultaneous patch clamp, while the registered scope also retains real calcium imaging. Exact archive files/version, full collection inclusion and native export manifest remain unresolved.

cohort.description: Figure 3d describes 4,982 frames from the 1,000-Hz mouse L2/3 example, 1,000 displayed pixel traces and a separate n=100-pixel correlation comparison in Figure 3f. Their exact pixel identities and independence are not recovered; this is not 100 independent neurons or animals. Calcium collection identity also remains to be bound.

split.description: Methods treat the full input stack as a sample for self-supervised temporal-window training (default 100 epochs). Preserve the source allowance for unlabeled same-stack adaptation and protect electrophysiology/reference labels. The local recording-disjoint split disallowing test-stack adaptation is a separate extension.

inputs.description: Same raw fluorescence stack, imaging frame rate/exposure and permitted spatiotemporal context as source FAST; synchronized electrophysiology is an evaluator comparator, not a candidate training target. Synthetic clean traces belong only to the source simulation controls.

preprocessing.description: Recover original ROI/pixel selection, fluorescence baseline definition, electrophysiology synchronization, temporal context, overlap handling, clipping and full-frame support. The local fixed-ROI/F0 rules are explicit prospective choices; paper weight decay 1e-4 and pinned README 0.9 are not silently interchangeable.

metric.description: Figure 3f uses Pearson correlation r=sum((x-xbar)(y-ybar))/sqrt(sum((x-xbar)^2)sum((y-ybar)^2)) between single-pixel ΔF/F and synchronized electrophysiology. Figure 3b analogously compares simulated traces with clean truth; image PSNR/SSIM and throughput are distinct outcomes.

aggregation.description: Exact pixel-level source summaries and baseline numeric correlation are not recovered. Report source strata separately; pixel/frame correlations cannot justify animal-level confidence, and prospective ROI/recording/group means cannot be substituted for the paper reduction.

comparison.primary_metric: Original Figure 3f denoised-fluorescence/electrophysiology Pearson correlation, with source fidelity and speed constraints; exact aggregate unresolved

published_baseline.description: Main text reports increased correlation and P<0.001 but no verified numeric FAST Figure 3f correlation aggregate was recovered. Figure 1d reports 1100.45 FPS for a 512×192×5000 stack on RTX A6000; that auxiliary throughput is not a denoising-quality score.

reproduced_author_baseline.description: Pinned training/inference code supplies a source route, but no source-matched FAST output/trace/score has been executed or qualified here. The prospective evaluator does not establish native same-stack parity.

minimum_effect.rationale: A meaningful correlation/fidelity gain must exceed source-measurement and replay variability while retaining spike timing/amplitude and declared real-time constraints. No numeric gain or allowable fidelity regression has yet been justified.

uncertainty.method: Recover original sampling units and predeclare paired source-recording contrasts with temporal dependence retained. A source-compatible descriptive pixel comparison can be reported, but an improvement uncertainty rule must not count correlated pixels/frames as independent biological repetitions.
uncertainty.independent_unit: Independent recordings/biological preparations where available; temporally dependent observations and pixels within one recording remain clustered.
uncertainty.rationale: The source n=100 pixel comparison supports a within-recording summary, not 100 independent biological samples; repeat runs alone quantify algorithm variability.

paper_win_requires: Recover the exact real-recording author baseline, original pixel/ROI roster, preprocessing, correlation aggregation and permitted same-stack training protocol.
Compare candidate and FAST on identical original recordings and label access, with predeclared meaningful temporal-fidelity gain and valid uncertainty.
Preserve original real calcium and voltage scope; synthetic controls or a favorable selected pixel/recording cannot replace it.
Retain spike fidelity, matched temporal context and hardware-bound end-to-end resource measurements; faster inference or smoother traces alone are insufficient.
Treat the existing group-disjoint evaluator as an extension unless exact source equivalence is independently established; changed splits never count as original-task victory.

current_sota.description: No current-SOTA claim; surpassing this source paper and surpassing later methods are separate source-verified comparisons.

episode.improvement_loop: Inactive until source comparison is recovered. Development may tune denoising with source-permitted raw-stack self-supervision and declared validation feedback; electrophysiology and clean synthetic final targets remain evaluator-owned.
episode.candidate_freeze: Seal denoiser/training code, all context windows, source-allowed adaptation rule, checkpoint selection, ROI/baseline recipe and timing boundary before final target comparison.
episode.final_evaluation: Replay the author and frozen candidate on identical complete original-recording support and source preprocessing, reporting real voltage, calcium and synthetic controls separately. Measure matched-hardware latency/throughput without substituting it for fidelity.
episode.baseline_policy: Source-paper FAST values, newly reproduced FAST values and local prospective evaluator outputs remain separate. No raw-input baseline or group-disjoint extension can replace the source FAST comparator.

blocking_issues: Exact numeric real-voltage FAST correlation baseline and original summary unavailable in reviewed main text/code.
Original pixel/ROI roster, ΔF/F baseline, synchronization and full archive file/version mapping unresolved.
Registered real-calcium plus real-voltage coverage not established by existing prospective panel.
Author Methods versus pinned configuration and native temporal/output handling need reconciliation.
Source-compatible evaluator, meaningful effect, dependence-aware uncertainty and fixed access/resource budgets remain unqualified.

legacy.notes: Preserve trace/fidelity/latency evaluator and its prospective-v1 split honestly as measurement/calibration and extension material. Its engineering tests and new split cannot award a source-paper win.
